newsitem.title: USA: Third of births in U.S. to unmarried women - study.
newsitem.headline: Third of births in U.S. to unmarried women - study.

text.p: Almost one-third of American children are born to unmarried women and the United States has one of the highest rates of teenage childbearing in the industrialised world, according to research released Wednesday.
Americans start having sex younger than they did 30 years ago, but the fertility rate has remained stable, a book from the Population Council reported.
The book is called "Fertility in the United States: New patterns, New Theories," with contributions from authors in the fields of economics, sociology, anthropology and psychology.
The Population Council is a non-profit group established in 1952 with the goals of improving reproductive health and achieving a balance between population and resources.

In the early 1970s, 45 percent of women who became pregnant while not married and who bore the child, married before the child's birth, compared with only 27 percent of women in the late 1980s, according to the book.

Each year, almost 1 million teenage women -- 11 percent of all women aged 15 to 19 years old -- become pregnant, according to the Alan Guttmacher institute on reproductive health; 54 percent of those pregnancies end in births.
Of the more than 4 million births in the United States in 1993, 30 percent were to unmarried women.
The researchers said the fertility rate has remained at about replacement level, or two parents having two children.
Researchers found that although American teenagers start having sex at similar ages to their counterparts in other countries, they do not use contraceptives as much.

"This is traceable to a social environment that romanticizes sexual activity but makes responsible sexual behaviour difficult," said one of the book's contributors, sociology professor S. Philip Morgan of the University of Pennsylvania.
Researchers said early intercourse was more common among black Americans, among those whose mothers have less education and among those not living with both parents at age 14.
